title: Acceptance and quality management — Ostrander & Lee CPAs
instructions: Ostrander & Lee is a CPA firm that audits private companies under AICPA standards and has adopted SQMS Nos. 1 and 2. Select the most appropriate response to each situation.

exhibits.title: Situations
exhibits.content:
1. A prospective audit client's management refuses to acknowledge in the engagement letter its responsibility for internal control. No law requires the audit.
2. Near the end of fieldwork, a client asks to change the audit to a review because its bank no longer requires an audit. The auditor has found no matters suggesting the request is improper.
3. The partner who led last year's audit of a listed-company subsidiary is proposed as this year's engagement quality reviewer on the same engagement.
4. The firm's monitoring process finds that several audit files lacked documentation of inventory observations.
5. Fees from one audit client have grown to 18% of the firm's total revenue.

rows.label: 1. Refusal to acknowledge responsibilities
options: Accept and note the refusal in the report
Accept and obtain the acknowledgment orally
rows.explanation: AU-C 210: if management won't acknowledge its responsibilities, the auditor should not accept the engagement unless required by law.

rows.label: 2. Request to change to a review
options: Agree if justified; the review report doesn't mention the audit
Refuse, because an engagement can't be changed once it has started
Agree, and describe the incomplete audit in the review report
rows.answer: Agree if justified; the review report doesn't mention the audit
rows.explanation: A change in circumstances affecting the need for the service is a reasonable basis for changing; the new report doesn't refer to the original engagement.

rows.label: 3. Proposed engagement quality reviewer
options: Acceptable, because the partner knows the client well
Not acceptable until a two-year cooling-off period has passed
Acceptable if the audit committee consents
rows.answer: Not acceptable until a two-year cooling-off period has passed
rows.explanation: SQMS No. 2: a former engagement partner should not serve as EQ reviewer on that engagement until two years have passed.

rows.label: 4. Monitoring finding
options: Evaluate severity, find the root cause and remediate
No action is needed if the audit opinions were appropriate
Report the finding to the state board of accountancy at once
rows.answer: Evaluate severity, find the root cause and remediate
rows.explanation: SQMS No. 1 requires the firm to evaluate findings, determine whether they are deficiencies, investigate root causes and remediate.

rows.label: 5. Fee concentration
options: Independence is impaired, so the firm must resign the client
A self-interest threat; evaluate it and apply safeguards
No threat exists, because the client is a private company
rows.answer: A self-interest threat; evaluate it and apply safeguards
rows.explanation: Significant fee dependence creates a self-interest threat under the conceptual framework; the firm evaluates its significance and applies safeguards, such as a pre-issuance review.
